note: REPLACES AN INFERENCE FROM AN OLDER FLEET. The previous value of 0.35 was read off an earlier year's generation mix, and the Thar fleet then ramped - Thar Energy, ThalNova and Lucky all entered service - so by the FY2023-24 anchor year the mine-mouth plants dominate coal generation. The old note also contradicted its own value: it classified Lucky Electric as Thar lignite, a reading under which 0.35 is too low for any year in the ledger. The residual IS Lucky: its name states no origin, so the bounds published by the runner are Lucky-as-imported (0.752) and Lucky-as-Thar (0.835), and 0.79 is their midpoint. Corroboration: weighting plant coal MASS by IPCC rank NCVs instead gives 0.70-0.84, overlapping the generation route. The 12 percent uncertainty spans the union of both routes - 10 was first tried and failed the covering test against the NCV route's lower bound of 0.698. See plant_ledger.coal_blend and outputs/power_coal_blend_fy2023_24.csv.

source: IPCC 2006 GL Vol 2 Ch 1 s1.4.1.2: net calorific value is about 10 percent below gross for natural gas
note: IPCC emission factors are defined on a NET calorific basis, so a gross heating value must be converted before the factor is applied. Omitting this step would overstate the category by 11 percent. The same net-basis requirement is what power_params.toe_to_tj documents as this sector's largest unresolved risk on the grid side.
